description: Telecom service cancellations including phone, internet, cable TV, and bundled services. Regulated by FCC at federal level with additional state PUC oversight.
typical_barriers: Claims customer is in contract period
Requires extended hold times or department transfers

email_1.subject: Cancellation of Service — Account: {{account_identifier}}
key_points: Clear cancellation request with account details
If past contract period, state so explicitly
If ETF claimed, reference applicable consumer protection law
Request written confirmation and final bill
telecom_specific_points: Equipment return: request clear instructions and deadline
Final bill: request that final bill reflect cancellation date, not end of billing cycle
If bundled: specify which services to cancel
Port number out if keeping phone number

email_2.subject: Follow-Up: Service Cancellation — SECOND REQUEST — Account: {{account_identifier}}
key_points: Note continued charges or lack of confirmation
Reference credit card dispute for unauthorized charges

email_3.subject: Final Notice: Service Cancellation — Account: {{account_identifier}}
key_points: State intent to file FCC complaint
State intent to file state PUC complaint
State intent to dispute charges with bank/credit card

federal.name: FCC Consumer Complaint Center
federal.description: File a complaint about phone, internet, or TV service. FCC forwards to the company and requires a response within 30 days.

notes: Telecom is regulated at both federal (FCC) and state (PUC) levels. FCC complaints are effective — companies must respond within 30 days. Early termination fees are a major barrier but may be challengeable if service was degraded or terms changed. Equipment return is a common post-cancellation issue.
